submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the head noun of a quantity phrase (numeral or 'few/many/just' + noun, e.g. 'two months', '12 miles', 'five points', 'just days') when the phrase sits where no object is expected, after a copula, an intransitive verb, a comma or a complete clause, so that it can only be an adverbial measure of distance, time or margin for a following relation word (from, after, before, ahead, west, tall, late). The noun's identity barely matters ('300 bricks tall' fires like '300 feet tall'), the same quantity as a direct object ('took/spent/wasted two hours') stays near zero, and a weaker secondary peak falls on a comma that closes a complete clause before a trailing participial or appositive modifier (', killing', ', followed by', ', opening'); there is no per-prompt floor, since sentence-initial and ordinary tokens are ~0.
